tone_patterns: Analytical and explanatory tone that frames sustainability topics as business-relevant (e.g., access to finance, cost of capital) rather than purely values-driven
Balanced presentation of positives and negatives, explicitly distinguishing actual vs potential effects
Risk-management language emphasizing controls, processes, and mitigation mechanisms
Forward-looking framing using time horizons (short/medium/long term) to structure implications
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short purpose statement describing what the section covers and the lens used for assessment
Uses definitional or scoping sentences to clarify value-chain segment boundaries (e.g., upstream) before discussing impacts
Progresses from general approach (strategy/process) to specific mechanisms (how it is done), then to illustrative examples
Includes bridging sentences that connect risk mitigation to opportunity creation (e.g., diversification reduces risk and enables new funding sources)
Ends with a concise summary of management approach, often transitioning into a numbered list of actions
heading_patterns: Numbered subsection headings combining a section index with a descriptive title
Headings include both the management theme (strategic management) and the scope (across value chain)
Standalone micro-heading introducing a specific assessment area (e.g., assessment and management of a value-chain segment)
Topic label and chapter numbering appear near the footer/header area to reinforce navigation
table_patterns: Two-part tabular layout separating 'impact materiality' from 'financial materiality' within the same page/section
Matrix-style tables with mirrored columns for positive vs negative (impact) and risks vs opportunities (financial)
Each row uses: item label + brief description, followed by a categorical qualifier column (e.g., actual/potential or timeframe)
Time horizon is presented as a discrete field (not embedded in prose), enabling quick scanning
Consistent phrasing pattern for entries: short title followed by a colon and a one-sentence explanation
Tables prioritize readability with short, modular statements rather than long paragraphs
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Numbered callout list (1–3) used as a compact process/controls diagram rather than a narrative paragraph
Each callout contains a short action statement; the set collectively represents a management framework
Diagram title explicitly states the assessed area and whether it covers risks, opportunities, or both
pdf_layout_patterns: Page header includes the thematic section label and a topic identifier (e.g., chapter/topic number) for wayfinding
Footer includes page number and report title line for consistent document navigation
Tables occupy the majority of the page width with clear column separation and aligned row structure
Use of whitespace and line breaks to keep each table entry visually distinct, supporting scanability
A new page begins with a prominent subsection heading followed by a short introductory paragraph before detailed content
Numbered callouts are arranged vertically with ample spacing, functioning as a sidebar-style summary block
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses IFRS-style framing: identifies risks and opportunities, specifies value-chain location, and links to financial effects
Employs cautious qualifiers (e.g., may/can) when describing potential outcomes, and more definitive language for actual outcomes
References internal assessment basis by pointing to earlier sections for methodology or identified enterprise risks/opportunities
Describes management approach in terms of processes, adherence, and periodic communication rather than promotional claims
States alignment/eligibility principles for use-of-proceeds or allocation approaches in a policy-like manner
evidence_presentation_patterns: Provides illustrative examples of instruments/mechanisms as evidence after describing the overarching strategy
Uses time-bounded or period-referenced examples to ground the narrative (without relying solely on qualitative statements)
Explains how funds/resources are managed post-raising/allocation using a clear rule-based description (e.g., alignment within a defined window)
Connects examples back to stated objectives (e.g., ensuring alignment with original goals and broader societal needs)
section_specific_observations: Strategy section blends materiality outputs (impact and financial) with value-chain risk/opportunity management narrative
Materiality is operationalized through categorical qualifiers (actual/potential; timeframe) rather than lengthy justification text
Value-chain discussion emphasizes upstream financing access as a strategic lever and frames governance/ethics as enabling conditions
The section uses a layered structure: materiality table(s) → narrative explanation → management actions diagram
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organization names, subsidiary names, country references, or stakeholder group identifiers unique to the reference
Any specific financial instruments, issuance descriptions, or claims of being the largest/first/leading
Any monetary amounts, dates, or cumulative totals
Any specific funding counterparties (e.g., types of institutions) if presented as factual relationships rather than generic categories
Any specific beneficiary groups or project types listed as funded outcomes
Any exact phrasing of risk/opportunity titles or impact statements
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Company and group names and report title references
Specific page numbers and section numbering tied to the reference document’s internal structure
Specific financial amounts and years associated with capital raising examples
Named financial instruments and issuance details presented as factual events
Lists of specific funded project categories and beneficiary segments
